issues.response: Confirmed, and thank you for refusing to invent a label. A prepared dose's label was answered once, by POST /mar/{mar_id}/prepare, and no read could give it again. From fixed_in on (compare overview's server_build with fixed_in): (1) GET /mar/{mar_id}/dose-label (new, ipd.mar.administer, logged as a read of the record) answers the same PrintOut as the preparation, built from what the preparation recorded (who prepared it, when, what it is diluted in), whoever prints it and whenever, marked REPRINT on the label with fields.reprint true. It prepares and gives nothing. (2) DOSE_NOT_PREPARED (409, new): the dose has not been prepared (prepared_at null): prepare it. (3) The preparation's own label is built the same way from the record, so the two are identical except for the mark (fields.reprint false on the first). The mar screen lists the call with a new UX rule (a new checklist item): 'Reprint label' on a prepared dose; never prepare again to get a label, never rebuild one on the terminal, and no key or label kept on the terminal is needed. The medication-safety playbook says the same. Regenerate your types (DoseLabelFieldsOut gains reprint; the error codes gain DOSE_NOT_PREPARED). The same update changes migrations (decisions 56-59), so the DEV server is reinstalled with fresh hospital data (your registry account stays) and your ward 15, bed 48, patient 17, admission 18, drug 12 and their orders and MAR rows are gone. To check it: prepare a dose of your own, end the app's session, reopen the MAR: 'Reprint' answers the label marked REPRINT, equal to the first but for the mark; on a dose not prepared: 409 DOSE_NOT_PREPARED.

Confirmed, and thank you for checking the exact refusal. The PRN route shares its checks with a scheduled dose through medication/administration.py, and the check that keeps every route's error list complete followed only a route's own module, so it missed them. From fixed_in on (compare overview's server_build with fixed_in): (1) POST /admissions/{admission_id}/mar/prn names every refusal it shares: PATIENT_IDENTITY_REQUIRED, PATIENT_IDENTITY_MISMATCH, DRUG_MISMATCH, HIGH_ALERT_CHECK_REQUIRED, ADMINISTRATION_VARIANCE_REASON_REQUIRED, SELF_ADMINISTRATION_INVALID, ADMINISTRATION_NOT_AUTHORIZED, and MEDICATION_ORDER_STOPPED (new, #45), MEDICATION_ORDER_INVALID, REFERENCE_NOT_FOUND. (2) The check now follows calls into other modules too. It found 51 more routes with an inherited refusal they did not name; each names them now: ICD_CODE_UNKNOWN on the six routes that take ICD codes, MSDS_CATEGORY_NOT_CONFIRMED on the inspection pack, ICD_SYSTEM_NOT_LOADED on the ICD browser, the roster refusals on editing, copying and swapping duties, OVERPAYMENT and INVOICE_LOCKED on the payment routes, INVOICE_HAS_PAYMENTS on cancelling a paid imaging or lab order, PATIENT_IDENTITY_MISMATCH on receiving a lab sample, the reagent refusals on a lab result correction, and others. The rest were checked unreachable and recorded with the reason. It also found a bug: cancelling a duty refused a person who had left, so their future duties could not be cancelled; a cancellation now checks only the planner's scope. (3) A backend test fails on any such refusal left unnamed. Re-run screen_test_plan for the screens you built: get_endpoint lists more codes; handle each by its code. Your identity check stays as it is. The same update changes migrations (decisions 56-59), so the DEV server is reinstalled with fresh hospital data (your registry account stays) and your ward 15, bed 48, patient 17, admission 18, drug 12 and their orders and MAR rows are gone. To check it: get_endpoint for POST /admissions/{admission_id}/mar/prn lists PATIENT_IDENTITY_REQUIRED.

Confirmed, and thank you for proving it with a live nurse client. We had found this kind of gap with #43 and fixed it across the backend before your report arrived, in the same update: every event a screen lists now reaches a role working on it. From fixed_in on (compare overview's server_build with fixed_in): medication.order.updated also goes to medication.safety.view, which the ward and ER nurses hold (and the doctors, the head nurse and the pharmacists), so the nurse who took a verbal order sees its countersignature without polling. The payload is unchanged (prescription_id, prescription_number, prescriber_id, change: VerbalOrder, Countersigned, QueryRaised, QueryAnswered or QueryWithdrawn, query_id): refresh the verbal orders list on it; countersigned_at stays authoritative. You need no other permission. A backend test now fails on any screen event its own roles do not receive. The same update changes migrations (decisions 56-59), so the DEV server is reinstalled with fresh hospital data (your registry account stays) and your ward 15, bed 48, patient 17, admission 18, drug 12 and their orders and MAR rows are gone. To check it: your exact journey with the nurse's terminal open: as demo.doctor countersign: medication.order.updated (change Countersigned) arrives and the list shows it signed.

Confirmed, and thank you for isolating the destination. The database refused self-administration on every line of an outside (ExternalMarket) prescription, though every description named only the route and the high-alert rule; a clinic without a pharmacy issues every inpatient line that way. The owner decided (decisions 59): a medicine bought outside may be self-administered under the same rule. From fixed_in on (compare overview's server_build with fixed_in): (1) POST /prescriptions and POST /prescriptions/verbal accept self_administration true on an inpatient's ExternalMarket line that names a drug of the hospital's list (drug_id): an oral, inhaled or topical medicine that is not high-alert, as for the hospital pharmacy. (2) A typed external_drug_name is never self-administered: 422 SELF_ADMINISTRATION_INVALID, because its high-alert status is unknown. (3) The complete rule, in the route's description, the field's description, the error's text and the medication-safety playbook: an inpatient order (IPD or Code Red); route Oral, SL, Topical, Inhaled, Ophthalmic, Otic or Nasal; not high-alert; on an outside line, a drug_id. The printed self-administration policy (PHC portal) says the same. Offer the self-administration switch on an outside line only when a listed drug is chosen. The same update changes migrations (decisions 56-59), so the DEV server is reinstalled with fresh hospital data (your registry account stays) and your ward 15, bed 48, patient 17, admission 18, drug 12 and their orders and MAR rows are gone. To check it: your two requests on a new synthetic admission: ExternalMarket with drug_id and self_administration true answers 201; the same line with only an external_drug_name answers 422.

Confirmed, and thank you for finding the supported path and asking for it to be named rather than guessing. A PRN line is not on the MAR until its first dose, and the MAR screen named no read that lists it; the master summary and the prescription detail work, but they hold every prescription of the patient, which the terminal would have to filter. From fixed_in on (compare overview's server_build with fixed_in): (1) GET /admissions/{admission_id}/mar/prn-orders (new, ipd.mar.view, logged as a read): the admission's active PRN lines (its inpatient orders, not stopped, cancelled or ended), each with prescription_item_id, the order (prescription_id, prescription_number, destination), drug_name, strength, dose_text, route, interval_hours, instructions, high_alert_category, lasa_with, self_administration, start_at, end_at, prescriber_name, last_given_at and given_last_24h. (2) The mar screen lists it with a new UX rule (a new checklist item): 'Give a PRN dose' picks the line there and shows the interval, the last dose and the doses of the last 24 hours; never a typed id. (3) Checking it found a gap: a PRN dose of a stopped or cancelled order was charted; it now answers MEDICATION_ORDER_STOPPED (409, new, details.field prescription_item_id) and nothing is charted: refresh the list. The inpatient-and-discharge playbook (MAR) says the same. The MAR routes moved to their own module; no path changed. Regenerate your types (PrnOrderOut is new). Replace the master-summary path with the new list. The same update changes migrations (decisions 56-59), so the DEV server is reinstalled with fresh hospital data (your registry account stays) and your ward 15, bed 48, patient 17, admission 18, drug 12 and their orders and MAR rows are gone. To check it: as demo.doctor prescribe a PRN line for a synthetic admission of your own; as demo.nurse the list shows it with last_given_at null; give one PRN dose: last_given_at set and given_last_24h 1; demo.doctor stops the line: the list is empty and a PRN dose answers 409 MEDICATION_ORDER_STOPPED.

Confirmed, and thank you for the exact request on a booking of your own and for keeping the rule as it is. The refusal comes from the database's guard on the operative note, and the check that keeps every route's error list complete read the Python services only, so it missed it. From fixed_in on (compare overview's server_build with fixed_in): (1) PUT /ot/bookings/{booking_id}/operative-note names OT_BOOKING_STATE_INVALID (409, not retryable): the note is written once the operation has started, on an InProgress, Cleaning or Completed booking (not Requested, Scheduled, EmergencyHold or Cancelled); nothing is saved. Offer the note only from the start of the operation, and on the refusal read the booking again. (2) Checking the theatre's other records the same way found the same gap, now named with the states: PUT pre-op-note (Requested, Scheduled, EmergencyHold or InProgress), PUT pre-anaesthesia (also before the sign in), PUT anaesthesia-record (Scheduled, EmergencyHold, InProgress, Cleaning or Completed; and OT_PRIVILEGE_REQUIRED for an anaesthetist without the privilege), POST recovery (Cleaning or Completed); OT_RECORD_FINAL on the anaesthesia record's vitals and events once it is signed and on a repeated pre-anaesthesia signature; OT_PRIVILEGE_REQUIRED on signing the anaesthesia record and on the recovery discharge; OT_BOOKING_NOT_ACTIVE on scanning and reversing consumables. (3) The surgical-care playbook gains a table of the booking states each part of the record accepts. (4) A backend test now reads the database's guards on the surgical record and fails on a route that does not name one of their refusals (each exception a code the route's operation never reaches, with the reason), and another makes your exact request. The database's refusals outside the theatre are not swept automatically yet: report any unlisted code you meet, as you did. Handle these by their codes on the theatre screens you build (surgical_record_surgeon, anaesthesia_record, pre_anaesthesia_clinic, recovery boards, OT consumables). Nothing about the rules changed. The same update changes migrations (backend issues #41, #42), so the DEV server is reinstalled with fresh hospital data (your registry account stays) and your ward 14, bed 46, patient 15, admission 16 and booking 1 are gone. To check it: as demo.surgeon book a synthetic operation for a synthetic admission of your own: PUT operative-note on the Requested booking answers 409 OT_BOOKING_STATE_INVALID; once the booking is started (InProgress) the same PUT answers 200. Re-read get_endpoint for PUT /ot/bookings/{booking_id}/operative-note.

Confirmed, and thank you for proving it with two live clients and real worker events. The worker sent vitals.due to ipd.flowsheet.record only, the nurses who record vitals, though doctor_inpatients lists the event. From fixed_in on (compare overview's server_build with fixed_in): (1) vitals.due goes to everyone who reads the flowsheet (ipd.flowsheet.record or ipd.flowsheet.view): the nurses as before and the doctors, without any recording permission; its payload is unchanged (admission_id, patient_name, bed_label, due_at, overdue_minutes). get_event('vitals.due') shows the new audience. (2) doctor_inpatients has a new UX rule (a new checklist item): vitals.due for one of my patients marks its vitals due or overdue (overdue_minutes) and, when the flowsheet is open, re-reads GET /admissions/{admission_id}/flowsheet (is_overdue); the server decides due and overdue, the nurse records, and the doctor's screen has no recording. A doctor receives it for every inpatient: show it for your own patients (and those waiting for a doctor) only. No polling and no guessed alerts: the event is the refresh signal. The inpatient-and-discharge playbook (ward nursing, vitals) says the same. Checking every screen the same way found 13 more listings of an event the screen's own roles never received; the same update fixes them: ot.booking.updated reaches ot.booking.view (the theatre nurses, the anaesthetists), critical_result.updated diagnostics.critical.view (the wards, the ER, the lab admin), medication.order.updated medication.safety.view (the ward that took a verbal order), blood.consent.withdrawn and blood.reaction.reported blood.bank.operate (the blood bank's technicians); ot.emergency_hold left the Code Red screen (the theatre's alarm: the answer carries ot_booking). A backend test now fails on any screen event no role working on it receives. Re-read get_event for those you use. In the same update the OPD re-route (workflow §1.4) gains GET /opd-queues/doctors, the doctors who see an OPD queue: re-route and slips go only to them. The same update changes migrations (backend issues #41, #42), so the DEV server is reinstalled with fresh hospital data (your registry account stays) and your ward 10 and admission 10 are gone. To check it: repeat your journey on a new synthetic admission with both clients open; the doctor now receives vitals.due when the nurse does.

Confirmed, and thank you for using a patient of your own and reassigning nobody. The Code Red stamped whoever pressed the button as primary_doctor_id, so a triage nurse's Code Red named her as the treating doctor, and no call designated or changed the treating doctor afterwards. The owner decided (decisions 57): a Code Red's treating doctor is a doctor. From fixed_in on (compare overview's server_build with fixed_in): (1) POST /admissions/code-red sets primary_doctor_id to the caller only when the caller is a doctor registered with the PMDC (clinical, PMDC, a number on file); a triage nurse's Code Red answers primary_doctor_id and primary_doctor_name null, and GET /admissions/{admission_id} shows null until a doctor takes the patient over. (2) The first doctor to record its reason and provisional diagnosis (POST /admissions/{admission_id}/admission-details, already required before the clinical discharge) becomes its doctor; a Code Red that has a doctor keeps them. (3) The handover you asked about (new, decisions 58): POST /admissions/{admission_id}/treating-doctor {doctor_id, reason} with an Idempotency-Key takes effect at once: the treating doctor hands over (Handover), any PMDC doctor gives an admission without one its doctor (TakeOver), the Hospital Admin or a Director reassigns while the treating doctor is away (Reassigned, new permission ipd.admission.reassign); anyone else answers TREATING_DOCTOR_ONLY (403, new). GET /admissions/{admission_id}/treating-doctor answers the doctor and every change (who, when, kind, reason; the take-over of (2) included); GET /ipd/treating-doctors lists the live admissions and their doctors (doctor_id; waiting=true: those without one); admission.doctor_changed (new) moves the patient between the rounds. doctor_inpatients lists the three calls, GET /staff/lookup and the event; the owner's dashboard has a new screen, treating_doctors. (4) POST /admissions refuses a primary_doctor_id that is not an active doctor registered with the PMDC: VALIDATION_ERROR (422, details.field primary_doctor_id), nothing created. (5) doctor_inpatients has new UX rules (new checklist items): my patients are those whose primary_doctor_id is mine; a Code Red with null shows to every doctor under 'Waiting for a doctor'; 'Hand over' and 'Take this patient'; never show the person who pressed Code Red as the doctor. code_red adds 'Doctor: waiting'. The inpatient-and-discharge playbook (Code Red; the treating doctor and its handover) says the same. Regenerate your types (TreatingDoctorOut, DoctorChangeOut, TreatingDoctorIn are new). The same update changes migrations (decisions 56, 58), so the DEV server is reinstalled with fresh hospital data (your registry account stays) and your ward 9, patient 8 and admission 9 are gone. To check it, on a synthetic ward and bed of your own: as demo.triage a Code Red for a new synthetic patient answers primary_doctor_id null; as demo.doctor admission-details makes demo.doctor its doctor; demo.doctor hands it to demo.doctor2 with a reason; GET .../treating-doctor shows TakeOver then Handover. Re-read get_screen_bundle('doctor_inpatients').

Confirmed, and thank you for stopping at the 403 instead of typing or guessing an id. The accounts (billing_admin) hold estimate.view, estimate.prepare and estimate.explain but not ipd.admission.view, and the screen listed the chart's GET /admissions/{admission_id}/transfers, which also carries the clinical reason for each move. Rather than give the accounts chart access, the estimate staff now read the moves with their estimate permissions. From fixed_in on (compare overview's server_build with fixed_in): (1) GET /cost-estimates/admissions/{admission_id}/moves (new; estimate.view, estimate.prepare or estimate.explain) lists every move of the admission, oldest first: transfer_id, the from and to ward (id and name), from_daily_rate and to_daily_rate, rate_changed, transferred_at, estimate_explained (a ChangeOfWard estimate for the move was explained) and the move's latest estimate that is not cancelled (estimate_id, estimate_status: open a Draft rather than prepare another). It never carries the reason for the move, the bed labels or who moved the patient. NOT_FOUND for an admission that does not exist. (2) cost_estimates_billing and cost_estimates_admissions list it in place of GET /admissions/{admission_id}/transfers, which stays the chart's list on the ward-transfer screens (ipd.admission.view, unchanged). (3) Both estimate screens have a new UX rule (a new checklist item): the move of a ChangeOfWard estimate is the worklist item's transfer_id or one picked from the new list; never a typed id, and never the chart's list. The cost-estimates-and-tariff playbook (section 3, step 3) says the same. This fix changes no permission or rule of POST /cost-estimates: a transfer_id of another admission still answers VALIDATION_ERROR. Regenerate your types (EstimateMoveOut is new). Checking every screen the same way found 21 more calls a screen's own roles could not make; they are fixed in the same update (decisions 56; re-read the bundles of the screens you have built). One of them changes a migration (the triage nurse reads a patient's documents), so the DEV server is reinstalled with fresh hospital data (your registry account stays) and your admission 7 is gone. To check it: as demo.admissions give a synthetic admission of your own a bed and move it (POST /admissions/{admission_id}/transfer, ideally to a ward with another daily charge); as demo.billing, GET /cost-estimates/admissions/{admission_id}/moves answers 200 with that move and GET /admissions/{admission_id}/transfers still answers 403; prepare the ChangeOfWard estimate with its transfer_id and the move shows estimate_status Draft; cancel your estimate afterwards if you do not explain it. Re-read get_screen_bundle('cost_estimates_billing') and get_endpoint for the new endpoint.
